memory_update.text: NEXA is a priority underfollowed Layer 1 candidate for the sulphuric-acid node because it is a NYSE-listed zinc smelter with explicit sulphuric-acid byproduct production in Latin America.

ITFS is a speculative_shadow candidate: OTCQX-listed Itafos has direct Conda sulphuric-acid dependence and a newly amended Rio Tinto Kennecott supply contract, but market cap, liquidity, and contract economics need verification.

For this node, separate net acid producers, net acid consumers, and contract-protected consumers; the same commodity shock can help smelter-acid sellers while hurting phosphate or SX-EW operators without pass-through.

Need a later pass on US-listed logistics/terminal names; Interacid, Trammo, Gulf Transport, and many sulphuric-acid logistics assets appear private or subsidiaries, so public-market mapping remains incomplete.

HWKN should be tracked as an underfollowed chemical-distribution candidate for sulphuric-acid availability, but survival depends on proving material acid volumes, pass-through pricing, and customer exposure.

KEX is a logistics hypothesis: useful if acid/sulphur route disruption increases demand for specialized US bulk-liquid barge capacity, but sulphuric-acid-specific cargo evidence is not yet established.
Smelter-acid producers can flip from environmental byproduct processors into strategic suppliers when merchant acid is scarce; TECK and SCCO provide US-listed examples for further mapping.

Need a dedicated search pass for OTC/ADR and non-US-listed acid logistics assets such as Sumitomo/Interacid, Stolt-Nielsen, Odfjell, Aurubis, Korea Zinc, and regional sulphur terminals, because US-listed coverage may miss the purest infrastructure nodes.

MMLP is the highest-node-purity US-listed discovery candidate found for sulphur/sulphuric-acid logistics and production, but it is a below-USD-300M speculative exception requiring liquidity, leverage, and contract-quality checks.
HWKN should be tracked as an underfollowed USD 1B+ chemical-distribution candidate with sulphuric-acid exposure, but acid materiality is unproven and must be verified in filings.
TGB is not a sulphuric-acid supplier; its relevance is acid-dependent SX/EW copper production at Florence, where fixed-price acid coverage and supply duration are the key hidden variables.

Need a follow-up pass on private or non-US-listed sulphuric-acid traders and terminal operators such as Interacid/Sumitomo, Trammo, Aglobis, and regional acid terminals because many chokepoint assets may sit outside the US-listed universe.

Add CGIFF/Chemtrade as the highest-priority underfollowed US-tradable sulphuric-acid candidate for this node; verify 2026 acid pricing and volume sensitivity before upgrading from inference to stronger claim.

Add ITFS/Itafos as a small-cap customer-dependency case tied to Rio Tinto Kennecott sulphuric acid; thesis can be positive if contract secures supply/cost, negative if index exposure raises raw-material pressure.

For this node, the most underappreciated public-market mapping may be not only acid producers but also who has secured acid contracts, who can monetize byproduct smelter acid, and who controls chemical-tanker or terminal capacity on replacement routes.

Need a follow-up search focused specifically on vessel-level acid logistics: Japan/Korea smelter acid exports, Chile/Indonesia importers, chemical tanker fixtures, terminal operators, and whether any US-listed tanker names carry sulphuric acid.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expansion found one obvious copper reference name and three more underfollowed or second-order US-listed exposures tied to sulphuric-acid production, procurement, or fertilizer input sensitivity. The strongest underfollowed candidate is Nexa Resources because it is a NYSE-listed zinc smelter with sulphuric-acid byproduct exposure. Itafos is a more speculative OTCQX discovery candidate because its Conda phosphate operation has explicit sulphuric-acid dependence and a recently amended Rio Tinto Kennecott supply contract. Mosaic is a larger but still node-relevant fertilizer customer whose phosphate margins may be sensitive to sulphur and sulphuric-acid costs. Southern Copper is included only as a high-attention reference anchor because it produces sulphuric acid and operates SX-EW copper assets, but its mega-cap status makes it less suitable for the underfollowed lane. Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around the sulphur/sulphuric-acid chokepoint. The strongest underfollowed candidates are not necessarily miners; they sit in chemical distribution, inland/coastal liquid logistics, and byproduct-acid smelting. The provided Kpler context frames the shock as a 2026 acid/sulphur trade-route disruption affecting Chilean copper SX-EW, Indonesian HPAL nickel, and fertilizer supply. Candidates below are research leads only, not recommendations; several require contract-level verification before advancing to later Serenity layers.
